anatomy.flutter: Menubar(menus: List<MenubarMenu>) builds a Focus-wrapped Container(h-8 border rounded-lg) > OverflowBox > Row of _MenubarTrigger widgets, each a Popover(anchor: MenuPointerDown(trigger text), content: MenuContent(children, indicatorSide: MenuIndicatorSide.start)) — one MenubarMenu per {label, children: List<MenuChild>}.
anatomy.web: Menubar > MenubarMenu > MenubarTrigger + MenubarContent (Portal-wrapped Radix MenubarPrimitive.Content), with MenubarItem/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/RadioGroup/Label/Separator/Shortcut/Sub/SubTrigger/SubContent all present with data-slot attributes, matching the Dart's shared-Menu-body row model one for one.

api.flutter: Menubar takes only menus: List<MenubarMenu>{label, children: List<MenuChild>} — a flat declarative list, no per-trigger disabled, no onOpenChange callback, no value/defaultValue controlled-open API.
api.web: MenubarPrimitive.Root/Menu/Trigger/Content are Radix primitives taking Radix's own value/onValueChange, loop, dir props plus per-item disabled via MenubarItem's inherited Radix Item disabled prop.
api.note: This mirrors the documented menu-family decision (see menu.json): Flutter's Menubar is a simplified declarative wrapper over the same MenuChild rows, while the web is raw Radix MenubarPrimitive with its full prop surface. The web is strictly more capable (controlled open state, per-item disabled) which is expected for an installable Radix-backed component versus Flutter's composed widget.

states.flutter: menubar.dart's doc comment records 'DOCUMENTED DRIFT (menus drift 1): the triggers overflow the bar they sit in. The root is h-8 with p-1, which leaves a 24px content box, and each trigger is h-8 — 32... Reproduced exactly: the port lets the row overflow rather than clipping it, because the reference writes no overflow-hidden.' Menubar.height is a fixed h-8 constant and _MenubarState wraps the Row in OverflowBox to reproduce that overflow.
states.web: components/ui/menubar.tsx's Menubar root class is now `flex min-h-8 items-center gap-0.5 rounded-lg border p-1` (line ~20) with an inline comment: 'min-h-*, not h-*: a fixed height is a ceiling as well as a floor, and the bar has to be able to grow with its triggers' text.'
states.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The web source has changed from the fixed h-8 the Dart file's doc comment describes (and which motivated the OverflowBox reproduction of 'drift 1') to min-h-8, a floor rather than a ceiling — the bar now grows with tall trigger content instead of clipping/overflowing. Flutter's Menubar.height constant and its OverflowBox-based overflow reproduction are now stale relative to the current web behavior; this is a real divergence, not a documented platform difference, since the web changed after the Flutter port measured it.

disabled.flutter: menubar.dart has no per-trigger or per-item disabled concept beyond MenuItem.enabled (defined in menu.dart, reused here via MenuChild); no menubar-specific disabled path exists.
disabled.web: MenubarTrigger has no disabled prop of its own in menubar.tsx; MenubarItem inherits Radix's disabled the same way MenuItem does in menu.dart. ADDED 2026-09-11 (gaps-closing pass, for menu-family parity): MenubarItem, MenubarCheckboxItem and MenubarRadioItem now also take disabledReason?: string, wired the same way as ContextMenuItem/DropdownMenuItem — components/ui/disabled.tsx's Disabled in mode="aria" (Radix's menu Item has no native disabled attribute to carry), giving an always-on aria-describedby plus a click/tap-reachable popover beside the row.
disabled.note: Disabled handling for menubar rows is entirely delegated to the shared menu-item mechanism already covered in menu.json's disabled dimension (gap: no reason/tooltip prop on the web side); there is no menubar-specific disabled behavior to audit separately, so this dimension is n/a here rather than duplicating that finding. ADDED 2026-09-11: this dimension pointed at menu.json's disabled dimension for the shared finding ("no reason/tooltip prop on the web side"); that finding no longer holds — all three menu-family item shapes carry disabledReason now, closing the drift this gaps brief named directly: 'a reason that exists on one menu and not its siblings is a gap that will be reported next audit.' menu.json itself is outside this pass's owned file set and is left for its own audit pass to update. Measured in the dev server (http://localhost:3111, desktop-dark): focusing a disabled item with disabledReason reads the reason via aria-describedby, and the info button opens a Popover on click/Enter/Space. Pinned by test/menubar.test.tsx and e2e/gaps-disabled.spec.ts.

interaction.flutter: _MenubarState._step handles ArrowLeft/ArrowRight to move the open menu between triggers ('ArrowLeft / ArrowRight on the strip — measured moving from "Users" to "Wallet" with the content following'), and _hover switches the open menu on pointerover with no intent delay ('Hovering a sibling while a menu is open switches instantly — no intent delay, no close animation'); barrier: PopoverBarrier.nonModal documents 'modal={false} — Radix's menubar is non-modal, which is the whole reason a sibling trigger can be hovered while a menu is open.'
interaction.web: Radix MenubarPrimitive supplies the same roving-focus ArrowLeft/ArrowRight-between-triggers and hover-to-switch behavior natively (non-modal by default), which is exactly what the Dart _step/_hover methods and barrier: nonModal setting port from measuring this file's underlying Radix primitive.

semantics.flutter: MenuMotion.slideSides and animateOut: false are passed into the Popover backing _MenubarTrigger's content, with the doc comment stating 'DOCUMENTED DRIFT (menus drift 2): MenubarContent has no exit animation. Its class list ends at data-open:zoom-in-95; the data-closed:animate-out data-closed:fade-out-0 data-closed:zoom-out-95 trio... is simply absent.' [Popover.animateOut] false is coded as that missing twin.
semantics.web: components/ui/menubar.tsx's MenubarContent className (around line 75) now reads '...data-open:animate-in data-open:fade-in-0 data-open:zoom-in-95 data-closed:animate-out data-closed:fade-out-0 data-closed:zoom-out-95' — the exit-animation trio the Dart doc comment says is absent is present in the current source.
